purpose: Efinaconazole is used to treat fungal nail infections, also called onychomycosis, which affect the toenails. It helps clear up the infection and allows healthy nail to grow back. It is applied directly to the affected nail, so it works right where the problem is.
how_it_works: Efinaconazole works by blocking something the fungus needs to build its outer protective shell, called its cell membrane. Without this protection, the fungus cannot survive and eventually dies off. Think of it like taking away the building materials the fungus needs to stay alive.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are mild and happen right where you apply it. These can include redness, flaking, peeling, or a little swelling or itching around the nail area. Some people may also notice blisters or pain near the treated nail.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, since the safety for babies has not been fully established. Do not swallow this medication and keep it away from your eyes, nose, and mouth. This medicine is for external use only on the nails. Keep it away from open flames as it is flammable.
typical_dosing: You apply efinaconazole solution once a day directly to the affected toenail(s) using the built-in brush applicator. Make sure to coat the entire nail, including under the tip if possible. Treatment usually lasts 48 weeks, so patience is important since nails grow slowly.
